problem.text: For a positive integer $n$, let $d_n$ be the units digit of $1+2+\cdots+n$. Find the remainder when $$\sum_{n=1}^{2017} d_n$$ is divided by $1000$.

steps.title: Where to start: compute the first few $d_n$
steps.body: Adding $2017$ digits one by one is hopeless, but units digits usually repeat in a cycle. So compute the first few values of $d_n$, the last digit of $1 + 2 + \cdots + n$, and watch for a pattern. Keep a running total and only track its last digit.

steps.title: The cycle has length $20$
steps.body: Going from $d_n$ to $d_{n+20}$ adds the $20$ numbers $n+1, \ldots, n+20$. Their last digits run through $0$ to $9$ twice, which adds $2\cdot 45 = 90$, ending in $0$. So the units digit comes back to the same value, and the digits $d_n$ repeat with period $20$. (Ten steps is not enough: $45$ ends in $5$.)

steps.title: Add up one full cycle
steps.body:
The full cycle is
$$1, 3, 6, 0, 5, 1, 8, 6, 5, 5, 6, 8, 1, 5, 0, 6, 3, 1, 0, 0.$$
Its sum is the building block for the whole problem.

your_turn.prompt: What is the sum of these $20$ digits?
your_turn.answer: $70$ (the first ten add to $40$ and the last ten add to $30$).

steps.title: Count full cycles and leftovers
steps.body: Since $2017 = 20\cdot 100 + 17$, the sum is $100$ full cycles followed by the first $17$ terms of one more cycle, $d_1$ through $d_{17}$. Careful: the leftover part starts again at $d_1$, not where the list left off.

your_turn.prompt: How much do the $100$ full cycles add, and what is that modulo $1000$?
your_turn.answer: $100\cdot 70 = 7000$, which leaves remainder $0$ when divided by $1000$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The first $17$ terms are the whole cycle minus $d_{18} + d_{19} + d_{20} = 1 + 0 + 0$, so they add to $70 - 1 = 69$. The total is $7000 + 69 = 7069$, and the remainder when it is divided by $1000$ is $69$.
